<!-- Generated by docs-site/scripts/split-threat-model.mjs from threat-model.md in consealdev/conseal (https://github.com/consealdev/conseal/blob/main/threat-model.md). Change the model there and run the script again. -->

The properties in this document hold **only if** these are true:

| # | Assumption | If it isn't |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The app is served over **HTTPS** with a valid certificate | A network attacker can serve a malicious JavaScript bundle |
| 2 | The app enforces a **strict Content Security Policy**, with no inline scripts or untrusted sources | XSS can call Conseal directly and use every key in IndexedDB |
| 3 | **Passphrases** have enough entropy, or a Secret Key is always used | Offline brute force against a stolen wrapped key becomes feasible |
| 4 | The **Secret Key** is never stored on the server or anywhere it can read | The defence against a compromised server ([§3.1](/docs/security/keys/#31-a-malicious-or-compromised-server)) collapses |
| 5 | The **mnemonic** is treated as a top secret, kept offline | One leak rebuilds the AEK |
| 6 | The app doesn't **eval** or run untrusted scripts in its origin | As 2: any script can use the loaded `CryptoKey`s |
| 7 | The browser's `SubtleCrypto` is **not compromised** | Every operation is the browser's; a backdoored browser breaks everything |
| 8 | `init()` runs before any `seal()` or `unseal()` that uses the stored AEK | `loadCryptoKey(AEK_KEY_ID)` returns `null`, and sealing throws on it. There is no fallback key |
| 9 | The app shows the **verification code** and approves a join only once the user confirms it matches | A server can swap the joining device's key and receive the AEK ([§4.5](/docs/security/circle/#45-what-it-relies-on)) |
| 10 | An app that runs the circle without `CircleClient` takes the **commitment before the key pair**, derives the approving device's code from **its own commitment**, and **finishes a join only once the codes are confirmed** | A server can answer a join itself and read everything the device seals ([§4.3](/docs/security/circle/#43-the-core-functions-without-circleclient)) |
| 11 | Collections where a stale value matters use a **merge policy that compares versions** | A dishonest server can roll records back unnoticed ([§6.3](/docs/security/sync/#63-what-a-dishonest-server-can-still-do)) |
